title: Mahler’s Adagietto: a melody takes its time
question: How much room can a conductor give each violin phrase without letting the Adagietto’s song come apart?
intro: Mahler writes for strings and harp, with a violin melody that keeps reaching across the bar-line. Mengelberg’s Concertgebouw players slide together between notes and press forward through the little pickups, then linger when the theme returns. The Peabody Symphony Orchestra supplies the second performance, drawn from its complete recording of the Fifth.

recordings.label: Peabody Symphony Orchestra
recordings.note: The strings and harp of the Peabody orchestra, heard within its complete recording of Mahler’s Fifth Symphony.

recordings.label: Willem Mengelberg, Concertgebouw Orchestra, 1926
recordings.note: The strings slide between notes together; Mengelberg urges the opening pickups forward and slows the returning theme.

passages.label: Violins above the harp
passages.note: The violins rise into the melody over plucked harp notes. The phrase leans on notes that take a moment to settle.

passages.label: The first great swell
passages.note: The violin line reaches higher, and the harp’s arpeggios spread beneath it. The phrase swells before turning down.

passages.label: The harp brings back the song
passages.note: The harp returns beneath the opening tune. Mengelberg begins this return more slowly, giving the familiar notes extra room.

passages.label: High violins, rising cellos
passages.note: High violins sustain the line while the cellos climb below. Mahler asks for broad bow strokes as the phrase approaches its last great swell.
